init.title: Polling and resilience
init.description: Tune how the SmartTub cloud API is polled. Defaults: interval 60 s, status timeout 30 s, reminders/errors timeout 20 s, command timeout 45 s, unavailable after 5 failed polls, back-off up to 600 s.

data_description.scan_interval: Seconds between polls when the API is healthy.
data_description.poll_timeout: Seconds allowed for the fullStatus call, which drives almost all entities.
data_description.aux_timeout: Seconds allowed for the reminders and errors calls. On failure the last known values are kept.
data_description.command_timeout: Seconds allowed for a command (jets, lights, temperature) including confirmation.
data_description.failure_threshold: The last good data is kept until this many polls in a row have failed. 1 = behaviour of the built-in integration.
data_description.max_backoff: While the API keeps failing, the poll interval doubles up to this value.

command_timeout.message: SmartTub did not respond to "{command}" within {timeout} s. The command may still be applied; the state updates at the next poll.

api_unreachable.title: SmartTub cloud API unreachable
api_unreachable.description: The SmartTub cloud API failed {failures} polls in a row (last error: {error}). Last successful poll: {last_success}. Entities are unavailable until the API responds again; the poll interval backs off automatically. This issue disappears after the next successful poll.

upstream_changed.title: Built-in SmartTub integration changed
upstream_changed.description: Home Assistant {version}: {reason}. Check the release notes to see whether the built-in integration now handles slow SmartTub API responses. If it does and you want to switch back, remove `custom_components/smarttub` (or the HACS repository) and restart; your entities and automations keep working because the domain and unique IDs are identical.
